svg.desc: Two panels from Hong and Stein's model at the baseline of their working paper's Table 1: news reaches the newswatchers on a fixed, linear timetable over 12 months, momentum traders hold for 12 months and use only the last price change, the news shocks have a standard deviation of 0.5 a month and the momentum traders' aggregate risk tolerance is 1/3, which gives an elasticity of 0.2605, the smallest covariance-stationary solution. Top, the cumulative price response to one unit of news by month, with the long-run value 1 dashed: with newswatchers alone it rises by 1/12 a month and reaches 1 in month 11; with momentum traders it peaks at 1.342 in month 12, falls back below 1 in month 22, reaches its lowest value after the peak, 0.885, in month 26 and is back above 1 in month 35. Bottom, the autocorrelation of monthly returns by lag: with newswatchers alone 0.917, 0.833, 0.750, ..., falling to zero at lag 12; with momentum traders 0.947, 0.850, 0.739, ..., positive up to lag 9 and negative from lag 10 to lag 22, lowest at −0.339 at lag 13. The parameters are the paper's; every number is this book's calculation, and the autocorrelations with newswatchers alone are this book's derivation.
